items.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: the last time that Richard Burton and Elizabeth Taylor worked together was a show called “Private Lives.”

ctx.x: Well I guess that means a lot of different things — jingles or just pop dates.

No I never did any of that. I did a Dixieland soundtrack for a race course commercial or something like that, that played on the local New York TV for a few weeks or months or something like that. And I did one thing with Warren Vache, the last time that Richard Burton and Elizabeth Taylor worked together was a show called “Private Lives.” Noel Coward’s “Private Lives.” It was on Broadway for about three weeks in 1983. And we were supposed to be the pit band. It was like a six piece jazz and sort of chamber jazz…
There’s a whole, I’m sure, crowd of musicians who make their living that way, in the studio pits.
